summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Gregor Johann Mendel (1856–1863) conducted hybridization experiments on garden peas (Pisum sativum). Key advantages: bisexual self-pollinating flowers, clear qualitative contrasting traits, and short life cycle. Mendel studied 7 contrasting traits located on Chromosomes 1, 4, 5, and 7. Monohybrid cross yields F2 phenotypic ratio of 3:1 and genotypic ratio of 1:2:1.

conceptBreakdown.content:
Gregor Johann Mendel established the bedrock of classical genetics through hybridization experiments on garden peas (*Pisum sativum*) from **1856 to 1863**.

### 1.1 The Seven Contrasting Traits of *Pisum sativum*

| Plant Trait | Dominant Character | Recessive Character | Chromosomal Location |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Stem Height** | Tall ($T$) | Dwarf ($t$) | **Chromosome 4** |
| **Flower Color** | Violet ($W$) | White ($w$) | **Chromosome 1** |
| **Flower Position** | Axial ($A$) | Terminal ($a$) | **Chromosome 4** |
| **Pod Shape** | Inflated / Full ($V$) | Constricted ($v$) | **Chromosome 4** |
| **Pod Color** | Green ($G$) | Yellow ($g$) | **Chromosome 5** |
| **Seed Shape** | Round ($R$) | Wrinkled ($r$) | **Chromosome 7** |
| **Seed Cotyledon Color** | Yellow ($Y$) | Green ($y$) | **Chromosome 1** |

### 1.2 Mendel's Core Laws of Inheritance

```
                            MENDEL'S THREE LAWS
                                     │
     ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                               ▼                               ▼
1. LAW OF DOMINANCE             2. LAW OF SEGREGATION           3. LAW OF INDEPENDENT ASSORTMENT
Characters controlled by        Alleles in a pair segregate     Alleles of two different genes
discrete factors (genes). In    during gamete formation so that segregate independently of one
heterozygotes, one dominates.   each gamete gets only ONE.      another during meiosis.
                                *(UNIVERSAL / NO EXCEPTION)*    *(Valid ONLY for unlinked genes)*
```

### 1.3 Monohybrid Cross Mechanics

$$\text{Monohybrid Cross: } TT \text{ (Tall)} \times tt \text{ (Dwarf)} \longrightarrow F_1: Tt \text{ (Tall)}$$

$$F_1 \text{ Selfing } (Tt \times Tt) \longrightarrow F_2 \text{ Phenotypic Ratio} = \mathbf{3:1} \text{ (3 Tall : 1 Dwarf)}$$

$$F_2 \text{ Genotypic Ratio} = \mathbf{1:2:1} \text{ (1 } TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt)$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: Emasculation and Bagging Protocol
conceptBreakdown.title: Emasculation and Bagging Protocol
conceptBreakdown.content: To prevent self-pollination in female parents, anthers are removed before dehiscence using forceps (Emasculation) and covered with a butter paper bag (Bagging) until stigma receptivity is reached.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Universal Purity of Gametes
conceptBreakdown.title: Universal Purity of Gametes
conceptBreakdown.content: The Law of Segregation is universal and has NO biological exceptions: heterozygous individuals (Tt) segregate pure gametes (50% T and 50% t) during meiotic anaphase I without any blending.
